F01.question: Q01 asks which ticket fields are populated.
F01.variables: TicketId, DisasterID, CollAddress, DebrisType, LoadDate, Volume, Lat, Lng, and ZoneName; measure: nonblank rows divided by 18,278 rows.
F01.interpretation: ID, incident, type, date, volume, and latitude/longitude are populated in all 18,278 rows. CollAddress is populated in 18,164 rows (99.38%). ZoneName is populated in only 6 rows (0.03%), so it cannot support a meaningful zone comparison.

F02.question: Q02 asks which basic quality checks flag records.
F02.variables: normalized CollAddress, parsed LoadDate, numeric Volume, Lat, Lng, TicketId, and TruckCapacity.
F02.interpretation: The only nonzero flag is 114 missing collection addresses. The checks found no unparseable load dates, missing or nonpositive CY values, out-of-range numeric coordinates, repeated TicketId values, or volumes above listed truck capacity.

F03.question: Q03 asks how recorded tickets vary by incident identifier and week.
F03.variables: DisasterID, local date derived from LoadDate, week beginning Monday, and ticket count.
F03.interpretation: DisasterID 84 accounts for 17,767 tickets; ID 80 accounts for 511. ID 84 therefore dominates the recorded activity in this extract.

F04.question: Q04 asks how recorded collection volume changes by day.
F04.variables: local pickup date from LoadDate and the daily sum of Volume in CY.
F04.interpretation: November 1, 2024 is the highest recorded day at 19,187.40 CY. The figure shows a strong early collection phase followed by lower recorded daily totals.

F05.question: Q001: How much pickup volume is recorded each day and week? Related gap check: Q006.
F05.variables: Local LoadDate and Volume. Sum CY by Monday-start week, including zero-record weeks. The first and last weeks are partial.
F05.interpretation: The week beginning October 28, 2024 has the most recorded CY (112,592.90). Three complete late-February/March weeks have no ticket rows. County reporting says the unincorporated-area final pass ended in mid-January 2025, making a wind-down plausible; the ticket file cannot establish the cause of a particular gap.

F06.question: Q06 asks how quickly recorded volume accumulated.
F06.variables: local LoadDate, daily summed Volume, and its running total in CY.
F06.interpretation: The running total reaches 644,952.65 CY by April 10, 2025. 483,862.65 CY, about 75.0% of this extract's total, was recorded before December 2024.

F07.question: Q07 asks how many load tickets were recorded each day.
F07.variables: local date from LoadDate and count of ticket rows or TicketId values.
F07.interpretation: November 1, 2024 also has the most recorded tickets: 525 loads. The peak in ticket count coincides with the peak in recorded CY.

F08.question: Q08 asks how recorded load sizes are distributed.
F08.variables: positive numeric Volume per ticket, grouped into 5-CY bins.
F08.interpretation: The median recorded load is 35.0 CY. The 20 to under 25 CY bin has 2,046 tickets, the largest bin. The maximum recorded load is 88.35 CY.

F09.question: Q09 asks whether ticket load sizes differ by debris type.
F09.variables: DebrisType and per-ticket Volume in CY; plotted types have at least 20 tickets.
F09.interpretation: Median loads are 35.0 CY for Vegetative/Woody, 37.7 CY for Construction & Demolition, and 32.3 CY for Veg Park Debris. These are differences in recorded load size, not evidence that one material was collected more efficiently.

F10.question: Q10 asks which debris categories contribute the most recorded CY.
F10.interpretation: Vegetative/Woody leads with 476,239.10 CY, followed by Construction & Demolition with 88,876.90 CY and Veg Park Debris with 71,562.35 CY.

F11.question: Q11 asks how each debris type's share of CY compares with its share of tickets.
F11.variables: DebrisType, summed Volume, ticket count, and each measure's percentage of its own total.
F11.interpretation: Vegetative/Woody accounts for 73.84% of CY and 75.29% of tickets. Its ticket share is slightly higher than its volume share, consistent with a slightly lower average load than the overall average.

F12.question: Q12 asks which material categories contributed to each week's recorded CY.
F12.variables: week from local LoadDate, DebrisType grouped as the top three types plus Other, and summed Volume.
F12.interpretation: Vegetative/Woody supplies most of the high-volume October and November weeks. In the peak week beginning October 28, its recorded volume alone is 104,988.55 CY.

F13.question: Q13 asks how the percentage mix of recorded CY changed by week.
F13.variables: week, top-three DebrisType categories plus Other, each type's weekly CY divided by total weekly CY.
F13.interpretation: Vegetative/Woody accounts for 81.7% of recorded CY in October–November but 50.3% from December onward. Veg Park Debris rises from 4.0% to 32.5% over those same periods, calculated from period totals. The composition of recorded tickets therefore changes substantially.

F14.question: Q14 asks whether recorded CY follows the ticket's capacity formula.
F14.variables: TruckCapacity, LoadPercent, calculated TruckCapacity × LoadPercent ÷ 100, and recorded Volume.
F14.interpretation: All 18,278 records align with the listed calculation at the displayed precision. The result suggests that Volume is calculated from capacity and fullness rather than being an independent measurement in this extract.

F15.question: Q15 asks where ticket coordinates cluster.
F15.variables: Lng, Lat, and count of tickets within each hexagonal cell (grid resolution 35).
F15.interpretation: All 18,278 records have numeric coordinates in the allowed latitude/longitude range. The densest plotted cell contains 974 tickets, centered near −82.714286°, 27.895000°. This is a concentration of recorded ticket locations.

F16.question: Q016: Where are the largest concentrations of recorded pickup volume?
F16.variables: Lng, Lat, and Volume summed within the same hexagonal grid as F15.
F16.interpretation: The highest-volume cell is centered near −82.714286°, 27.895000° and contains 46,453.90 recorded CY. High-CY cells broadly follow high-ticket-count clusters.

F17.question: Q17 asks how the footprint of recorded ticket coordinates changes by month.
F17.variables: LoadDate converted to month, Lng, Lat, and monthly ticket count.
F17.interpretation: 6,100 tickets are dated October 2024 and 8,012 November 2024; the mapped footprint is broad in those months. Later records become sparse, including 7 in March 2025 and 30 in April 2025.

F18.question: Q18 asks how often the same recorded address appears.
F18.variables: nonblank CollAddress normalized to uppercase with repeated spaces collapsed, ticket count per normalized address, and frequency buckets 1 through 9 and 10+.
F18.interpretation: The extract contains 11,033 normalized nonblank addresses. 2,890 have at least two tickets; 93 have ten or more. Repeated tickets are common enough to investigate as a normal operational pattern or a data-quality issue.

F19.question: Q19 asks how far apart distinct recorded dates are at a normalized address.
F19.variables: normalized CollAddress, local date from LoadDate, distinct address–date pairs, and days between successive dates; values of 60 or more days are grouped as 60+.
F19.interpretation: There are 1,576 intervals between distinct recorded dates, with a 3-day median. 582 intervals are exactly one day; 39 are 60 days or more. Short revisits occur frequently in the recorded data.

F20.question: Q20 asks which local dates have records and how many.
F20.variables: local date from LoadDate, weekday, Monday-start week, and daily ticket count.
F20.interpretation: Tickets appear on 141 of 191 dates in the observed span; 50 dates have no record in this extract. The calendar shows the timing of ticket reporting, including runs of higher and lower recorded activity.

F21.question: M04: How long does recorded ticket activity span in each Zone1 debris zone? Related area question: Q025.
F21.variables: Zone1, local LoadDate, Volume, TicketId. For each zone: first and last ticket date; first date cumulative CY reaches 90% of that zone's observed total.
F21.interpretation: Across 30 zones, the time to 90% of each zone's CY ranges from 32 to 122 days. The first-to-last ticket spans range from 53 to 187 days. These are recorded activity periods, not verified clearance times or municipality comparisons.

F22.question: Destination field: How much pickup-ticket CY is recorded under each DisposalSite label?
F22.variables: DisposalSite, Volume, TicketId. Sum CY and count tickets per destination label.
F22.interpretation: All 18,278 tickets have a destination label. SOD FARM SOUTH has the largest recorded sum at 289,309.45 CY. The label does not prove a load arrived there or show processing, recycling, or final landfill disposal.

F23.question: Recorded flow: Which Zone1 debris-zone and DisposalSite label pairs have the most ticket CY?
F23.variables: Zone1, DisposalSite, Volume. Sum CY for each zone–destination-label pair.
F23.interpretation: The matrix shows how recorded pickup CY is distributed among zone–destination-label pairs. It is a ticket-label flow view, not a verified chain of custody or final-disposal outcome.

F24.question: M01: Where is recorded pickup volume associated with each Contractor label?
F24.variables: Contractor, pickup Lat/Lng, Volume. Sum CY in identical hexagonal map cells for each label.
F24.interpretation: DRC and PINELLAS COUNTY are the only Contractor labels. The maps show the footprint of ticket locations by label, not verified crew coverage or subcontractor participation.

F25.question: Q032/Q035: Where are blank collection addresses and internally conflicting coordinate fields?
F25.variables: CollAddress (blank after whitespace trim), GPS text, numeric Lat/Lng, and Volume. A GPS conflict means either coordinate differs by more than 0.00001 degree.
F25.interpretation: 114 tickets have blank collection addresses (4,268.50 CY), and 1 ticket has GPS text differing from its numeric Lat/Lng. These flags do not verify whether any address is mapped to the wrong place (Q045).

F26.question: Q030: Which repeated address labels have unusually spread-out pickup coordinates? Q045 remains unresolved.
F26.variables: Whitespace-normalized CollAddress, Lat/Lng, TicketId. For labels with 10+ tickets, distance from each coordinate to that label's median coordinate; color shows 90th percentile in km.
F26.interpretation: 93 labels have 10+ tickets; 15 have a 90th-percentile coordinate spread above 1 km. Broad road and park labels can legitimately span large areas. Authoritative address geometry is needed before calling these GPS/address mismatches.

F27.question: M01: How many tickets, truck IDs, and recorded CY are associated with each Contractor label?
F27.variables: Contractor, TicketId, TruckNumber, and Volume. Sum CY, count ticket rows, and count distinct truck IDs per Contractor label.
F27.interpretation: DRC has 14,799 tickets and 608,886.10 CY; PINELLAS COUNTY has 3,479 tickets and 36,066.55 CY. The source has no separate subcontractor field, so subcontractor participation cannot be identified.

F28.question: M02: How many distinct truck IDs appear on tickets in each week, by Contractor label?
F28.variables: Local LoadDate (Monday-start week), Contractor, and distinct TruckNumber. A truck appearing on multiple tickets in one week counts once for that contractor.
F28.interpretation: The highest observed week begins October 28, 2024, with 142 distinct truck IDs. This is an activity count within the ticket extract, not verified total deployment, available fleet, hours, or shifts.

F29.question: M03: What is the distribution of listed capacity among truck IDs with pickup tickets?
F29.variables: Distinct (Contractor, TruckNumber) pairs and their consistent TruckCapacity values, binned into 10-CY ranges.
F29.interpretation: There are 283 distinct truck IDs: 183 DRC and 100 PINELLAS COUNTY. Listed capacity is a registration field, not measured payload. The file does not identify trucks that were deployed but generated no ticket.
